references.title: V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.2, printed pp. 49–55

items.title: The dihedral operation is a quandle

references.title: V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.2, printed pp. 49–55
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–5

items.statement:
For an odd prime $p$, let $\mathbb F_p=\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z$ and define
$a*b=2b-a$. Then $(\mathbb F_p,*)$ is a quandle.

items.title: Quandle colorings are invariant under oriented Reidemeister moves

references.title: V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 49–52
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–9
Józef H. Przytycki, 3-coloring and other elementary invariants of knots, §1, arXiv:math/0608172, pp. 2–3

items.statement:
Let $Q$ be a quandle and color regular oriented link diagrams by the normal-to-overarc
rule in the Definition. Every oriented Reidemeister move and planar isotopy induces
a canonical bijection between the two coloring sets. Consequently, under
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, diagrams of ambient-isotopic oriented links have bijective
coloring sets; if $Q$ is finite, their coloring counts are equal. Conversely,
suppose a set with a binary operation uses this crossing rule and every oriented
local R1, R2, and R3 replacement gives a unique coloring extension in both
directions for every boundary coloring. Then the operation is idempotent, every
right translation is bijective, and the operation is right self-distributive.
This converse requires local extension bijections, not equality of total
coloring counts alone. No claim that a coloring count classifies knots is made.

items.title: Racks, diagram fundamental quandles, and adjoint groups

references.title: V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.2, printed pp. 49–55
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §§2.1 and 2.2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8
Sam Nelson, Link invariants from finite racks, §§2.1–2.4, arXiv:0808.0029v3, pp. 2–6

items.statement:
A **rack** is a set $R$ with a binary operation $*:R\times R\to R$ such
that for every $y\in R$ the right translation $R_y(x)=x*y$ is a bijection
and $(x*y)*z=(x*z)*(y*z)$ for all $x,y,z\in R$. A **quandle** is a rack
satisfying $x*x=x$ for every $x$. For either structure, write
$x\mathbin{\bar *}y=R_y^{-1}(x)$.

For a regular oriented link diagram $D$, let $A(D)$ be its finite set of
maximal under-arcs. Form the set of finite terms recursively: each symbol
$x_a$ for $a\in A(D)$ is a term, and if $s,t$ are terms then $s*t$ and
$s\mathbin{\bar *}t$ are terms. Let $\sim$ be the intersection of all
equivalence relations on these terms that are compatible with both operations
and contain the quandle identities: idempotency, right invertibility, and
right self-distributivity, together with the crossing relations.
At a crossing with source and target under-arcs $u,v$ and overarc $o$, the
crossing relation is $x_v=x_u*x_o$; reversing source and target gives the
equivalent relation with $\bar *$. The quotient term set $Q(D)$ is the
**diagram quandle**, or the diagram presentation of the **fundamental
quandle**. Its independence of diagram is proved in the Theorem.

For any quandle $Q$, its **adjoint group** $\operatorname{Adj}(Q)$ is the
group presentation with generators $e_q$ for all $q\in Q$ and relators
$e_{q*r}=e_r^{-1}e_qe_r$ for all $q,r\in Q$. A group presentation
$\langle X\mid S\rangle$ means the quotient of the free group on $X$ by the
normal closure of the relator words $S$.

The diagram presentation and the adjoint group are algebraic constructions;
this definition makes no completeness or knot-classification assertion.

items.title: Compute dihedral Fox colorings by row reduction

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, 3-coloring and other elementary invariants of knots, §2, arXiv:math/0608172, pp. 10–11
V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 49–52
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8

items.statement:
Input a finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $a$ arcs and $c$ crossings,
fixed finite orderings of its arcs and crossings, and an odd prime $p$. The algorithm returns the full set
$\operatorname{Col}_p(D)$ of assignments of residues in $\mathbb F_p$ to the
arcs satisfying the Fox crossing equations, together with
$|\operatorname{Col}_p(D)|$.

1. Create one variable $x_j$ for each arc in the supplied order, and process
   crossings in the supplied order.
2. At each crossing with overarc $o$ and the two underarcs $i$ and $j$, append
   the homogeneous linear equation $2x_o-x_i-x_j=0$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
   At a crossing, add the coefficients of any repeated arc in that row.
3. Starting with the first column and first unused row, scan columns from left
   to right. In a column with a nonzero entry in an unused row, choose the
   first such row, swap it into the next pivot row, divide it by its nonzero
   pivot, and add multiples of it to every other row to clear that column.
   Advance the pivot row by one. If the column has no such entry, leave it
   free and continue to the next column.
4. After all columns have been processed, assign every free variable
   independently any value in $\mathbb F_p$ and solve the reduced equations
   for the pivot variables. Return each resulting assignment once and the
   number returned.

items.title: The rack kink map is bijective

references.title: Sam Nelson, Link invariants from finite racks, §§2.1 and 3, arXiv:0808.0029v3, pp. 2–7
V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 49–52

items.statement:
Let $R$ be a rack, with right translations $R_y(x)=x*y$. The kink map
$\pi:R\to R$, $\pi(x)=x*x$, is a bijection. Its inverse is
$\pi^{-1}(z)=R_z^{-1}(z)$.

items.title: Check a finite rack table and enumerate diagram colorings

references.title: Sam Nelson, Link invariants from finite racks, §§2.1, 2.2 and 3, arXiv:0808.0029v3, pp. 2–7
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8

items.statement:
Input an integer $m\ge1$, a table $T\in\{1,\ldots,m\}^{m\times m}$ with
entry $T[x,y]$ intended to be $x*y$, a mode "rack" or "quandle", a finite
regular oriented link diagram $D$ with $a$ arcs and $c$ crossings, and fixed
finite orderings of its arcs and crossings. If the table is not $m\times m$,
return invalid-table-shape with its row lengths. If an entry is outside
$\{1,\ldots,m\}$, return invalid-table-entry with its row, column, and value.
Otherwise perform these checks in order:

1. For each $y=1,\ldots,m$, check whether the column
   $(T[1,y],\ldots,T[m,y])$ is a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$. If not,
   return right-translation-not-bijective with $y$, a repeated value and a
   missing value.
2. For each ordered triple $(x,y,z)$ in lexicographic order, check
   $T[T[x,y],z]=T[T[x,z],T[y,z]]$. If not, return
   self-distributivity-fails with $(x,y,z)$ and both table values.
3. In quandle mode, check $T[x,x]=x$ for each $x$ in increasing order. If
   not, return idempotency-fails with $x$ and $T[x,x]$.

If the selected axioms pass, enumerate the $m^a$ functions from the supplied
ordered arcs of $D$ to $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ in lexicographic order. Retain an assignment
exactly when it satisfies the crossing rule in the rack/quandle Definition,
using the inverse column permutation when the rule calls for the right
division. Return the retained assignments and their number. No correctness or
complexity claim is part of this algorithm's Definition.

items.title: The Fox-coloring algorithm terminates and returns all colorings

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, 3-coloring and other elementary invariants of knots, §2, arXiv:math/0608172, pp. 10–11
V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 49–52
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8

items.statement:
For every odd prime $p$ and every finite regular oriented link diagram $D$,
the algorithm in the Definition terminates and returns exactly
$\operatorname{Col}_p(D)$. If its reduced system has $f$ free variables, it
returns $p^f$ colorings. It uses at most $a$ pivot steps and at most $ca$
row-entry elimination scans for a diagram with $a$ arcs and $c$ crossings.

items.title: The finite-table coloring algorithm terminates and is correct

references.title: Sam Nelson, Link invariants from finite racks, §§2.1–2.2, arXiv:0808.0029v3, pp. 2–5
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8

items.statement:
For $m\ge1$, a table on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, either rack or quandle mode, and
a finite regular oriented diagram $D$ with $a$ arcs and $c$ crossings, the
finite-table algorithm terminates. It reports the first failed table-format
condition or rack/quandle axiom with a witness; if every selected axiom holds,
it returns exactly all rack or quandle colorings of $D$, each once, and their
count. It performs at most $m^3+2m^2+2m$ row-shape, table-entry, and triple checks for the
format, rack, and quandle conditions and
tests at most $m^a$ arc assignments, each against the $c$ crossing rules.

items.title: Diagram fundamental quandles and adjoint groups from Wirtinger data

references.title: V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §5.2, printed pp. 52–55
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §§2.1–2.2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For a nonempty oriented link $L$, the diagram quandle presentations from any two regular oriented diagrams of $L$ are isomorphic by the local quandle Tietze transformations for R1, R2 and R3. If $L=K$ has one component and $D$ is its diagram, let
$$W(D)=\langle g_a\ (a\in A(D))\mid g_v=g_o^{-1}g_ug_o\text{ at every crossing with source }u,\text{ target }v,\text{ and overarc }o\rangle.$$
Then the positive-meridian Wirtinger constructor uses these same under-arcs and crossing relations, and
$$\operatorname{Adj}(Q(D))\cong W(D)\cong\pi_1(S^3\setminus K).$$
No completeness or knot-classification assertion is made.

items.title: Rack colorings are framed Reidemeister invariants

references.title: Sam Nelson, Link invariants from finite racks, §§2.1–2.2, arXiv:0808.0029v3, pp. 2–5
V. O. Manturov, Knot Theory, Chapter 5, §5.1, printed pp. 49–52
J. Scott Carter, A Survey of Quandle Ideas, §2, arXiv:1002.4429v2, pp. 3–8

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth framing statements. Let $R$ be a rack and let $\pi(x)=x*x$ be its kink map. Rack-coloring sets
are in bijection across every oriented R2 or R3 move and planar isotopy.
Across a single oriented R1 curl, the label transported along the affected
strand changes by $\pi$ or $\pi^{-1}$ according to the curl orientation.
Consequently, an opposite-kink pair on the same component whose two signed framing changes cancel
induces a bijection on colorings. A single unframed R1 move has a unique
extension for every boundary color exactly when $\pi$ is the identity, which
is the quandle idempotency axiom. Thus finite rack coloring counts are
invariant under R2, R3, planar isotopy, and framing-preserving opposite-kink
compensation; the unframed R1 move is covered when the rack is a quandle.

items.title: One Fox coloring prime does not classify knots

references.title: Józef H. Przytycki, 3-coloring and other elementary invariants of knots, §2, arXiv:math/0608172, pp. 10–11

items.statement:
For a fixed odd prime $p$, equality of the Fox $p$-coloring counts of two
knots implies that the knots are ambient-isotopic.
